topic: Union-tangent efficiency and oracle-adaptation frontier for identification-robust short-panel ATT estimation. Observe iid fixed-length panels with finitely many groups and finite-support covariates, overlap, bounded fourth moments, one final-period treated group, and no anticipation. Let the ATT be identified on the nonnested union of conditional parallel trends and a uniquely identified full-rank group-level synthetic-control mean restriction. At every intersection law with fixed rank and overlap margins, characterize the PT and SC influence-function classes and their intersection; derive the union convolution bound; prove simultaneous equality with both branch oracle bounds iff their canonical gradients coincide, and one-sided equality iff the relevant branch gradient satisfies the other branch's derivative constraints; compute the envelope by finite covariance-weighted quadratic programs; and construct a cross-fitted attaining one-step estimator with consistent variance and multiplier coverage uniform over root-n local alternatives in either branch. Include the equal-share three-group, three-period witness with mean paths (0,0,0), (-1,-2,-2), (1,2,2), independent bounded innovations, and control change variances 1 and 4, which yields SC weights (1/2,1/2) versus PT-efficient weights (4/5,1/5). Consumers are Rummo et al.'s 2026 sugary-drink-tax synthetic-comparison DiD and Sun–Xie–Zhang's Alaska minimum-wage application. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: With finite covariate support, each branch is a finite conditional-moment manifold. Starting from a common union-valid influence function, the presolve represented the branch influence-function classes as affine translates of their restriction-normal spans; their intersection reduces the union canonical gradient to a covariance-weighted projection, computed by one finite quadratic program per stratum. Pythagorean projection identities give the stated simultaneous and one-sided adaptation criteria. In the legal equal-share witness, independent final innovations retain distinct SC and PT coefficients, while SC weight-path terms occupy preperiod coordinates. Checks of rank boundaries, covariance degeneracy, weight boundaries, local sequences, and current literature found no refutation or exact collision, subject to the stated interiority margins. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove a uniform asymptotic-linear expansion for the estimated profiled-normal projection, including rank stability and multiplier validity along every root-n sequence contained in either branch. EARLY KILL TEST: Symbolically build the no-covariate three-period, three-group restriction-gradient Gram matrices and solve their intersection quadratic program. Stop if the common influence-function class is empty or the claimed strict coefficient gap fails; pivot to characterization-only if the solution is identically Sun–Xie–Zhang's influence function for every full-rank covariance design.

open_problems.open_problem: At fixed-rank, fixed-overlap laws satisfying both conditional parallel trends and the group-level synthetic-control restriction, characterize the common regular influence-function class and its union convolution bound, including necessary-and-sufficient conditions for simultaneous or one-sided equality with the branch-oracle bounds.

source_refs.claim: The paper identifies short-panel ATT under either of two nonnested PT and SC assumptions but develops its semiparametric and bootstrap theory separately under the two branches.
source_refs.author: Yixiao Sun, Haitian Xie, and Yuhang Zhang

source_refs.claim: The paper derives closed-form efficient influence functions for overidentified short-panel DiD under parallel trends, including covariance-optimal weighting, but has no alternative SC branch.
source_refs.author: Xiaohong Chen, Pedro H. C. Sant'Anna, and Haitian Xie

source_refs.claim: For a different finite-support semiparametric union model, the authors construct estimators efficient at the intersection where both nuisance submodels hold.
source_refs.author: Eric J. Tchetgen Tchetgen, James M. Robins, and Andrea Rotnitzky

source_refs.excerpt: Uniform local-oracle width achievability over arbitrary triangular unions ... remain open.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Sun–Xie–Zhang establish union-valid identification but derive different branch influence functions because their moment is orthogonal under PT and nonorthogonal under SC; Chen–Sant'Anna–Xie solve only the PT efficiency problem. The missing object is the tangent geometry of the nonconvex PT-or-SC model: regularity at an intersection law imposes both branches' derivative constraints, including SC-weight derivatives absent from the PT score. The prior CausalSmith result independently isolates an unresolved local-oracle adaptation boundary over a union, but its two-law width obstruction must be replaced here by root-n submodels in two conditional-moment tangent spaces. The first proof step is to derive the two restriction-normal spans in one observed-data Hilbert space and determine whether their affine influence-function classes intersect.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A convolution theorem expressing the union canonical gradient through a covariance-weighted projection onto the intersection of the PT and SC influence-function classes, finite-stratum quadratic-program formulas, iff criteria for simultaneous and one-sided oracle adaptation, and a strict equal-share three-group witness.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the exact short-panel motivation, the nonnested identifying assumptions, and the practical reason the analyst cannot select the correct branch.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: PT is credible when conditional trends align but SC is credible when stable donor weights exist -> neither assumption nests the other and applications cannot know which holds -> union-valid identification protects the ATT but yields branch-dependent influence laws -> characterize sharp union efficiency and the oracle-adaptation frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate PT into sequential conditional moments, derive the efficient influence function from their restriction normals, and solve the conditional covariance-optimal weighting problem.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the PT canonical gradient and covariance geometry forming one face of the proposed union projection.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct an optimal estimating function regular on a union model and prove semiparametric efficiency at its intersection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its finite-support union geometry is the closest published analogue of a common PT/SC influence function.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive the panel-DiD ATT efficient influence function and calibrate nuisance estimation so the asymptotic linear representation is doubly robust.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its influence function is the just-identified PT building block that the union characterization must recover on the PT face.

open_problems.open_problem: Prove a uniform asymptotic-linear expansion and uniformly valid multiplier confidence interval for an estimated union-efficient one-step ATT estimator along every root-n local sequence lying in either the PT or SC branch and approaching their intersection.

source_refs.claim: The paper proves multiplier-bootstrap consistency under PT and SC through separate branch arguments with different influence functions, but does not state uniformity over branch-switching triangular arrays.
source_refs.author: Yixiao Sun, Haitian Xie, and Yuhang Zhang

source_refs.claim: The authors obtain doubly robust inference with machine-learning nuisances but show that nonregular behavior may arise when only one nuisance component is consistently estimated.
source_refs.author: Oliver Dukes, Stijn Vansteelandt, and David Whitney

source_refs.claim: The paper develops cross-fitted doubly robust estimators with explicit fast remainder rates for semiparametric functionals.
source_refs.author: Whitney K. Newey and James M. Robins

source_refs.excerpt: does not furnish observable spectral substitution, a common-multiplier coupling, or uniform anti-concentration

open_problems.why_unsolved: Pointwise validity under each fixed branch does not control triangular arrays whose PT and SC violations approach zero at root-n scale, because the proposed influence function itself depends on estimated covariance matrices and profiled restriction normals. SC also has first-order weight-estimation terms absent under PT, matching the branch-dependent nonregularity warning in Dukes–Vansteelandt–Whitney. The prior CausalSmith calibration attempt records the analogous failure of population Gaussianization to provide observable spectral substitution, common-multiplier coupling, or uniform anti-concentration. Here the proof must jointly control cross-fit remainders, inverse-Gram perturbations, rank stability, the random projection map, variance estimation, and the conditional multiplier law over both local tangent cones.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving sqrt(n)(hat(theta)-theta)=n^(-1/2)sum_i phi_{P_n}(O_i)+o_P(1) uniformly over all admissible root-n PT-or-SC sequences, together with consistent plug-in variance and uniformly valid conditional multiplier coverage under fixed rank and overlap margins.

writing_exemplar.why: Its separate PT and SC limit theorems expose why one local-uniform inference theorem is still needed when the identifying branch is unknown.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: PT yields an orthogonal score -> SC introduces first-order weight-estimation effects -> one estimator and bootstrap are pointwise valid under either maintained branch -> inference near the intersection requires an expansion uniform over branch-switching local laws.

method_exemplars.technique: Use foldwise conditional expansions to remove own-observation bias and bound second-order products of nuisance-estimation errors.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired estimator is a cross-fitted one-step functional, with the new complication that its score contains an estimated projection.

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze inference when only one nuisance branch is correct and isolate the source of nonregularity despite double robustness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the closest proof template and warning for local sequences on which different restrictions become active.

method_exemplars.technique: Couple empirical processes to Gaussian and multiplier processes with explicit approximation errors and anti-concentration control.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its conditional coupling bounds can convert a uniform influence expansion into multiplier validity for the finite branch-and-stratum statistic vector.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop identification-robust short-panel ATT inference when the group-level SC mean matrix is locally rank-deficient or has more donor groups than preperiods, using penalized weights without sacrificing validity on the PT branch.

source_refs.claim: The paper's SC expansion requires a uniformly well-conditioned mean Gram matrix and identifies penalized semiparametric estimation with non-point-identified weights as an unresolved extension.
source_refs.author: Yixiao Sun, Haitian Xie, and Yuhang Zhang

source_refs.claim: Synthetic DiD uses regularized unit and time weights and establishes consistency and asymptotic normality under a latent-factor panel regime.
source_refs.author: Dmitry Arkhangelsky, Susan Athey, David A. Hirshberg, Guido W. Imbens, and Stefan Wager

source_refs.claim: The paper derives estimators, tests, and confidence sets valid across weak, semi-strong, and strong identification regimes.
source_refs.author: Donald W. K. Andrews and Xu Cheng

open_problems.why_unsolved: Sun–Xie–Zhang's SC influence expansion inverts the mean Gram matrix under a fixed positive eigenvalue margin, while regularized synthetic DiD operates in a different large-panel latent-factor regime. The target–method search found no treatment of fixed-length micro panels combining weakly identified SC weights with an alternative regular PT branch. The first proof step that changes is the linearization of the SC weights: the ordinary inverse derivative must be replaced by a singular-value-dependent, penalized, or set-valued derivative, after which the ATT may remain regular through PT even though the SC nuisance is weakly identified.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A local asymptotic experiment indexed by the drifting smallest singular value, together with a penalized union-valid ATT estimator and confidence set uniformly valid from rank failure through fixed-rank SC and root-n efficient under fixed rank.

writing_exemplar.why: It states the relevant fixed-length data regime, explains group-level SC weight identification, and locates rank and nonuniqueness at the proof boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Short panels identify group-level SC weights when preperiod rank is sufficient -> donor proliferation or collinearity can destroy that rank -> regularization stabilizes weights but changes local inference -> obtain ATT inference valid through rank failure while retaining the PT safeguard.

method_exemplars.technique: Partition the parameter space by identification strength, derive regime-specific local limits, and combine them into uniformly valid confidence procedures.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The drifting minimum singular value of the SC mean matrix is the direct analogue of their weak, semi-strong, and strong identification index.

method_exemplars.technique: Embed identification failure in a semiparametric local experiment and characterize weakly regular parameters through the derivative operator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: SC-weight nonuniqueness is a semiparametric rank failure while ATT can remain regular through the alternative PT branch.

method_exemplars.technique: Stabilize synthetic unit and time weights with ridge penalties and propagate their estimation into an asymptotic-normality proof.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the donor construction to adapt, although its proof must be rebuilt for fixed-length conditional moments and union validity.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize sharp short-panel ATT bounds and uniformly valid confidence sets when either a bounded violation of conditional parallel trends or a bounded misspecification of the group-level SC mean restriction is allowed, without knowing which approximation is valid.

source_refs.claim: The paper derives partial-identification regions and uniformly valid inference when post-treatment PT violations are bounded relative to observed pretrends.
source_refs.author: Ashesh Rambachan and Jonathan Roth

source_refs.claim: The paper shows that SC estimators can remain biased under imperfect pretreatment fit and develops diagnostics and guidance for demeaned SC.
source_refs.author: Bruno Ferman and Cristine Pinto

source_refs.claim: The paper supplies ATT identification under the nonnested union of PT and group-level SC, but both branch restrictions are exact.
source_refs.author: Yixiao Sun, Haitian Xie, and Yuhang Zhang

open_problems.why_unsolved: Rambachan–Roth relax PT without an alternative SC branch, whereas Ferman–Pinto analyze imperfect SC fit without combining it with conditional-PT sensitivity. Exact union robustness can be discontinuous when both restrictions fail slightly. The target–method search surfaced these separate literatures but no sharp combined region. The first proof step that changes is Rambachan–Roth's support-function calculation: it must optimize over the union of a PT-violation set and an SC residual-and-weight set while accounting for shared covariance and estimated-weight uncertainty.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp identified-set formula whose endpoints are values of finite convex programs over the two approximate branch sets, plus endpoint estimators and a confidence set uniformly covering ATT over prespecified PT-violation and SC-misspecification radii.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation converts unease about an exact identifying restriction into an interpretable sensitivity region with honest inference.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Exact parallel trends is unverifiable -> pretrends can discipline plausible post-treatment violations -> bounded violations partially identify ATT -> extend this sensitivity logic when either approximate PT or approximate SC may be valid.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent post-treatment bias restrictions as a convex set, compute support-function ATT bounds, and prove sharpness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: One component of the proposed union region is a PT sensitivity set; the new work adds the alternative SC residual set.

method_exemplars.technique: Expand SC bias under imperfect pretreatment fit and use demeaned weighting plus a specification statistic to track misspecification.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies an observable SC-fit discrepancy that can parameterize the second branch's sensitivity radius.

method_exemplars.technique: Bias-correct plug-in bound estimators and use Gaussian-process approximations for uniformly valid inference on optimization-defined endpoints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed ATT endpoints are values of finite programs whose active branch and constraints can change with the law.

open_problems.open_problem: For staggered adoption, derive the joint union-efficient influence function and simultaneous confidence band for the vector of group-time ATTs when each cohort-time cell is identified by either conditional PT or a cohort-specific full-rank SC restriction.

source_refs.claim: The paper extends PT-or-SC identification to staggered adoption by reducing each group-time ATT to a single-treated-group problem but does not derive a joint union efficiency bound.
source_refs.author: Yixiao Sun, Haitian Xie, and Yuhang Zhang

source_refs.claim: The paper derives PT-only efficient influence functions for staggered group-time ATTs and event-study aggregates.
source_refs.author: Xiaohong Chen, Pedro H. C. Sant'Anna, and Haitian Xie

source_refs.claim: The paper identifies group-time ATT under conditional PT and proves bootstrap validity for simultaneous inference over periods and cohorts.
source_refs.author: Brantly Callaway and Pedro H. C. Sant'Anna

open_problems.why_unsolved: Sun–Xie–Zhang's cellwise reduction does not solve the joint problem because donor pools, SC weights, group shares, and untreated outcomes are reused across cells, producing cross-cell derivative constraints and covariance terms. Chen–Sant'Anna–Xie solve the PT-only vector efficiency problem, while Callaway–Sant'Anna provide simultaneous inference without an alternative SC manifold. The target–method search found no joint union result. The first proof step that changes is to stack all cellwise restriction normals before projection; projecting each cell separately need not produce the canonical gradient of an event-time aggregate.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving the stacked union canonical gradient for all reported ATT(g,t) cells, the induced efficient gradient for event-time aggregates, covariance-weighted quadratic programs accounting for shared donors, and a valid multiplier simultaneous confidence band.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the standard cohort-time decomposition and explains why group-time effects and simultaneous bands are the building blocks of staggered-policy analysis.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Staggered adoption creates heterogeneous cohort-time effects -> group-time ATTs avoid contaminated aggregate comparisons -> simultaneous inference is required across the effect path -> make the entire vector efficient and identification-robust when either PT or cohort-specific SC holds.

method_exemplars.technique: Stack overidentified PT moments for cohort-time cells, derive covariance-optimal influence functions, and propagate them to event-study aggregates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It solves the full PT face of the proposed vector problem and shows why cellwise equal weighting is inefficient.

method_exemplars.technique: Form cohort-specific PT-or-SC moments with fixed donor pools and linearize the estimated SC weights.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the SC derivative for each cell; the new work must stack those derivatives and intersect them with the PT vector constraints.

method_exemplars.technique: Aggregate group-time ATT influence functions and apply a multiplier bootstrap for simultaneous inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its joint bootstrap construction matches the requested confidence band once the union-efficient stacked influence function is available.

literature_map:
Sun, Xie, and Zhang (2025, arXiv:2503.11375) are the exact anchor: short-panel ATT is identified under PT or group-level SC, while semiparametric and bootstrap arguments are separated by branch.
Their PT score is Neyman-orthogonal, whereas the SC law requires first-order corrections for estimated propensity ratios, conditional means, and SC weights.
Their multiplier bootstrap is valid under either maintained assumption, but no theorem is stated uniformly over root-n sequences approaching or switching across the intersection.
Their fixed-rank SC theory relies on stable inversion of the group-mean system; penalized inference with nonunique weights remains outside the established theory.
Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie (2025, arXiv:2506.17729) derive the PT-only short-panel efficient influence function and covariance-optimal weighting over preperiods and comparison groups.
Sant'Anna and Zhao (2020, Journal of Econometrics) provide the canonical panel-DiD ATT efficiency bound and doubly robust nuisance calibration.
Tchetgen Tchetgen, Robins, and Rotnitzky (2010, Biometrika) show in another finite-support union model that union robustness and local efficiency can coexist at an intersection.
Newey and Robins (2018, arXiv:1801.09138) provide cross-fitting remainder machinery, while Dukes, Vansteelandt, and Whitney (2024, JMLR) document nonregularity risks when only one nuisance branch is correct.
Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2016) provide multiplier and Gaussian coupling tools, but not for an estimated union-tangent projection.
Andrews and Cheng (2012, Econometrica) and Kaji (2021, Econometrica) supply local weak-identification theory relevant when the SC mean matrix approaches rank failure.
Arkhangelsky et al. (2021, AER), Abadie, Diamond, and Hainmueller (2010, JASA), and Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein (2021, JASA) develop SC weighting and regularization in regimes distinct from fixed-length micro panels.
Ferman and Pinto (2021, Quantitative Economics) establish persistent bias under imperfect SC fit, while Rambachan and Roth (2023, Review of Economic Studies) derive sharp PT-violation sensitivity regions and uniformly valid inference.
Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021, Journal of Econometrics) provide group-time ATT decomposition and simultaneous inference; Sun–Xie–Zhang extend union identification cellwise, but joint union efficiency remains untreated.
Searches for union-tangent ATT efficiency, PT/SC oracle adaptation, joint PT-SC sensitivity, weak-rank short-panel SC, and staggered vector union efficiency found no exact collision with the five retained opportunities.
